question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Barcoded lineage tracing with sister-cell splitting
ideas.description: Label cells with expressed lineage barcodes, split each population before drug, and compare survival and transcriptomes of sister clones to quantify heritability of persistence and recover pre-treatment states of future survivors via scRNA-seq of the untreated sibling arm.

ideas.title: Fluctuation test plus switching-rate modeling
ideas.description: Run Luria-Delbrück-style assays on many small clonal expansions, then fit stochastic models to separate pre-existing, rapidly switching states from drug-induced adaptation and estimate state switching rates and memory duration.

ideas.title: Live-cell imaging with retrospective fate mapping
ideas.description: Time-lapse image cells carrying reporters (cell cycle, stress response, mitochondrial potential) for days before and during drug, then trace survivors back to identify which pre-drug features predicted survival.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome of persisters with epigenetic perturbation
ideas.description: Profile chromatin accessibility and RNA jointly in untreated cells and persisters to identify reversible regulatory states, then test causality with CRISPRi/CRISPRa or epigenetic inhibitors of the top candidate regulators.

ideas.title: Pre-sorting by metabolic and mitochondrial state
ideas.description: Use FACS or FLIM to isolate cells by mitochondrial potential, NADH state, or lipid peroxidation susceptibility before drug exposure, then compare their survival to test whether metabolic heterogeneity causally drives tolerance.
